common_name: Elizabeth Ginger Lily (Tom Wood Salmon-Pink Hardy Ginger)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in spring after soil has warmed, in rich, evenly moist soil in a sunny to lightly shaded border with room for the towering stalks.

directions: Set rhizome divisions in spring in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full to mostly sun, allowing generous room for this Tom Wood hybrid to reach its imposing mature height. Beginning in midsummer, thick cane-like stalks are topped with large, honeysuckle-scented salmon-pink flower clusters that open continuously over several weeks and draw hummingbirds and butterflies. It is among the tallest and hardiest Hedychium coccineum hybrids grown outdoors, and established Gulf Coast clumps generally shrug off winter with a thick mulch layer even where top growth freezes back. Divide crowded clumps in early spring every few years to maintain strong, upright flowering canes.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Dr. Moy Variegated Ginger Lily (Speckled Hardy Ginger)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in rich, moist soil in bright partial shade; strong pseudostems generally need no staking.

directions: Plant rhizomes in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in bright partial shade to light morning sun, where the paint-splashed white speckling on each leaf shows to best effect against deeper shade. This Hedychium flavum x coccineum hybrid, discovered among a batch of seedlings and named for the San Antonio Botanical Garden botanist who raised it, remains the most widely grown variegated ginger lily and is notably more vigorous than typical variegated selections. Fragrant peachy-orange flowers with a darker orange throat appear on sturdy, self-supporting stalks in late summer and early fall. Divide congested clumps in early spring and remove any all-green reverted shoots promptly to keep the variegation strong.

common_name: Vanilla Ice Ginger Lily (Compact White-Flecked Hardy Ginger)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in rich, moist soil in bright partial shade; its smaller stature suits containers and tight garden beds.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, fertile soil in bright partial shade to filtered morning sun, where the heavy white fleck-and-streak variegation on each leaf stays crisp without scorching. A more heavily variegated sport of Hedychium 'Dr. Moy', this selection trades some vigor and height for denser white patterning, staying compact enough for smaller borders and large containers. Fragrant peachy-pink flower spikes open in late summer above the foliage, though the plant is grown primarily for its striking leaves. Cut out any vigorous, less-variegated reverted shoots at the base as soon as they appear to preserve the desirable coloring.

common_name: Pradhanii Ginger Lily (Giant Peach-Flowered Hardy Ginger)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in spring in rich, moist soil in a sunny to lightly shaded spot with plenty of room for a large, spreading clump.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to light shade, giving this vigorous old Indian hybrid ample room to form a dense clump of tall canes over time. From late summer until frost, each stalk is topped with a large spike of light peach flowers with honeysuckle fragrance, the throat deepening to yellow toward the petal tips, making it one of the longest-blooming ginger lilies in the Gulf Coast garden. Its exceptional vigor and prolific flowering have made it a mainstay of tropical-style plantings in the Southeast. Water generously through the growing season and mulch heavily over winter where clumps are left in the ground rather than lifted.

planting.note: Plant dormant rhizomes in spring once soil has warmed; flower spikes emerge from bare ground before the foliage each year.

directions: Plant rhizomes in humus-rich, well-drained soil in bright shade to nearly full sun with consistent moisture through the growing season. One of the tallest ornamental Curcuma species, it sends up striking two-foot, pine-cone-shaped bracts in bright pink topped with yellow flowers directly from the ground in late spring, well before the broad tropical leaves unfurl. Established clumps go fully dormant in winter and reliably resprout from the rhizome the following spring as long as the root zone stays unfrozen, making it a reasonably dependable perennial through zone 8 with a heavy winter mulch. Lift and store rhizomes indoors in colder zones or where drainage is poor and winters run wet.

common_name: Scarlet Fever Hidden Ginger (Red-Stemmed Ornamental Curcuma)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in spring in rich, well-drained soil; flower cones appear low at the base of the clump in spring before leaves expand.

directions: Plant rhizomes in fertile, well-drained soil in bright shade to morning sun with steady moisture through the growing season. Grown chiefly for its vivid red stems and the red midrib striping each pleated green leaf, this selection produces low, popsicle-shaped spring flower cones in pink and purple with green tips near the base of the clump before the foliage rises to five feet or more. It is somewhat hardier than many ornamental Curcuma and has persisted outdoors through mild Gulf Coast winters when planted in a protected, well-drained bed with heavy mulch. Where winters run cold or wet, lift rhizomes in fall and store them dry and frost-free until spring replanting.
